title: The Pego Theorem for the Hilbert--Schmidt Class
abstract: This paper establishes an operator-theoretic version of Pego's compactness theorem within the framework of quantum harmonic analysis on general locally compact abelian phase spaces. We show that a bounded set of Hilbert-Schmidt operators is precompact if and only if it is uniformly equicontinuous under phase-space shifts and its Fourier-Weyl transform is uniformly equicontinuous on the dual phase space. We provide applications to quantum physics.
summary: This work generalizes Pego's compactness theorem to the operator setting using quantum harmonic analysis. It provides a necessary and sufficient condition for a set of quantum operators to be precompact: the set must exhibit uniform equicontinuity both in the operator domain and in its Fourier-Weyl transform domain. This has direct applications in proving the stability of quantum states in quantum information and quantum estimation theory.
main_problem: The paper establishes an operator-theoretic version of Pego's compactness theorem within the framework of quantum harmonic analysis on general locally compact abelian phase spaces.
main_result: A bounded set of Hilbert-Schmidt operators is precompact if and only if it is uniformly equicontinuous under phase-space shifts and its Fourier-Weyl transform is uniformly equicontinuous on the dual phase space.
method: The proof relies on characterizing precompactness via the equivalence between operator equicontinuity and the equicontinuity of the Fourier-Weyl transform, leveraging properties of unitary isomorphisms.
model_or_system: The theory is applied to quantum information contexts, specifically analyzing families of thermal states and quantum state estimators in multi-mode systems.
key_observables: Quantum characteristic functions ($\chi_{ho}$), the Hilbert-Schmidt norm ($\|\cdot\|_{\mathcal{T}^2}$), and the Fourier-Weyl transform ($FU$).
important_parameters: Finite physical energy constraints ($ ar{n}_{\max} < \infty$) are used to ensure the precompactness of state families.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the existence of an irreducible projective unitary representation $(U, H)$ that is square-integrable, integrable, and strongly continuous.
paper_structure: The paper reviews classical $L^p$ precompactness criteria, introduces Quantum Harmonic Analysis (QHA) tools, states the central Quantum Pego Theorem, and then applies it to quantum information problems like thermal states and quantum tomography.
why_interesting: This provides a powerful, general mathematical tool (the Quantum Pego Theorem) to rigorously prove the stability and convergence (precompactness) of quantum state ensembles arising from physical measurements or thermalization processes.
